verdict.rationale: Both refactors look behavior-preserving: on a trace through each, the error variants, positions, empty-value handling and stop-after-error behavior all match the original. A also adds seven focused tests that lock in edge cases the existing suite never covered: separator errors, nested brackets, invalid and trailing escapes, stray quotes and empty values. For a refactor whose whole requirement is "exactly the same tokens and errors", those tests are the deciding factor. B's pure scan functions are slightly cleaner, but B leaves the edge cases unprotected once its temporary comparison is gone.
a_issues: State updates are split across helpers: `key_or_word` sets `Value`, `value()` resets to `Field` before scanning, and `finish_delimited` advances `pos` as a side effect. The state flow is harder to see than in a single place.
b_issues: No tests added. The untested edge cases (ExpectedSeparator, NestedBracket, InvalidEscape, trailing backslash, stray quotes, empty values) stay unprotected after the temporary comparison is discarded.
`next()` matches on `self.state` twice and has a separate end-of-line check, which is a bit awkward for a dispatcher.

verdict.rationale: Both refactors keep the original behavior. Tracing each scanner, I found the tokens, error variants, error positions, final `pos` and the stop-after-error rule all match the old code, and both stay byte-level with no allocation. B also adds seven focused tests for edge cases the old suite never covered: separator errors, nested brackets, invalid and trailing escapes, stray-quote positions and empty values. Those tests protect the refactor and any future change to this hot path. A rests its equivalence claim on a one-off random comparison that was not kept in the repository.
a_issues: Adds no tests, so the claimed equivalence is not protected by anything in the repository and future edits to the tokenizer stay unguarded.
`next()` matches on `self.state` twice and has a separate `State::Field && start >= len` check, which is slightly awkward for a dispatcher.
b_issues: State changes are spread across the helper methods: `value` sets `Field`, `key_or_word` sets `Value`, and `finish_delimited`/`bare` set `pos`. That makes the transitions a little harder to see than with pure scanners returning `(token, next_pos)`.
`value()` relies on `bare()` returning an empty token at a blank or the end of the line. This is correct but implicit.
